info.description:
## Overview
This document describes how to integrate with the Leafly Order API to receive and manipulate users' orders from leafly.com.

Leafly's Order API allows you to retrieve and update orders on behalf of retailers using your integration.

Notifications of order events occurring on leafly.com will be communicated to your system by webhooks.

### Getting Started
Integrating with the Leafly Order API requires you to have an existing integration with **Version 2.0** of the **[Leafly Menu API](https://docs.leafly.io/menu-integration-docs/v2.html)**.

When your menu integration is complete, contact us at **api-support@leafly.com** for order API sandbox access and credentials.

You will need to provide us with destination urls for each webhook event. They can be the same or different.

### Credentials
Credentials for interacting with the Leafly Order API include:
- One set of **[OAuth2 Client Credentials](https://oauth.net/2/)**, that is, a `Client ID` and `Client Secret`
- One `HMAC Key` for webhook authentication
- An `orderIntegrationKey` for each retailer using your integration

The OAuth2 credentials and HMAC key are unique to each integrator, while there is a unique `orderIntegrationKey` for each retailer managed through your integration.

#### API Roots Urls
- Sandbox: `https://reservations-api-sandbox.leafly.io/v1/order_integration`
- Production: `https://reservations-api.leafly.com/v1/order_integration`

#### Postman Collection
[View json in browser](https://docs.leafly.io/reservations-api/order-api/order_api.postman_collection.json)

[![Run in Postman](https://run.pstmn.io/button.svg)](https://god.gw.postman.com/run-collection/16702746-406b7fa7-e3d2-4883-b028-5191e1ff3fc7?action=collection%2Ffork&collection-url=entityId%3D16702746-406b7fa7-e3d2-4883-b028-5191e1ff3fc7%26entityType%3Dcollection%26workspaceId%3D87514285-801e-4833-8de6-2ea91a1e8d3a)

### Limitations
* Orders are only available for retrieval while live, or within twenty four hours of reaching a terminal state.
* Media associated with an order (e.g., government and medical id images) are only accessible before order acknowledgement and when the order is in pending status.
* Order update operations can only proceed after order acknowledgement.
* Pending and expired are valid statuses but are not valid values for the status update endpoint.
* API requests are rate limited, though sufficient headroom should exist for normal order volumes.

#### Payments
At present Leafly does not process payments for orders placed on its platform, and so provides no payment details through the Order API other than a possible indication of the customer's `paymentPreference`.

### Expectations
It is expected that
* Orders are acknowledged as having been retrieved in whole by your system within fifteen minutes of receiving an order submission webhook.
  Any orders not acknowledged by this deadline will be auto canceled.
* Order status updates correspond to an intuitive, smoothly progressing lifecycle. Not all statuses are required (as our systems might not have a clear 1:1 status mapping),
  but for example, supporting only direct movement to `picked_up` would not be allowed. Unless Leafly's outbound HMAC keys fails your validation,
  webhook requests should only be responded to with status codes 200 or 201. These webhook events are not the place to apply business rules or validations on the order lifecycle.
* Addition or substitution of new cart items into a user's order requires that referenced variants exist (that is, were submitted by your integration to the Leafly Menu API), and are in stock in the Leafly catalog.
* Order preview requests are interacted with in a synchronous fashion where the response body contains all validated fields.
* Leafly will be the sole originator of automated consumer facing communications related to orders placed on the Leafly platform. That is, Leafly shoppers should receive _no_ automated emails or text messages from a partner system with regard to order confirmation, status updates, etc.

### UberEats
It may be possible to qualify your order integration for use in the Leafly UberEats program in applicable markets.
  Be aware that any participating retailers will be beholden to additional operational expectations to maintain the desired customer experience.

The UberEats integration operates upstream of the Leafly Order API, and can be treated as black box from the perspective of Order API integrators.
  That is, your integration needn't be concerned about what happens between Leafly's and UberEat's systems.
  There are however, some behavioral changes to accommodate when interacting with Leafly's Order API in the UberEats context.

Additional integration requirements for UberEats:
* Must be able to communicate updates about the delivery portion of the order lifecycle (i.e., `out_for_delivery` and `arrived_at_customer`)
* Must be able to reliably accept cancelation notifications from UberEats that are forwarded to your system by Leafly.

Other behaviors:
* UberEats orders will show `"marketplace": "uberEats"` in the order details
* UberEats orders will show `"phoneNumber": null`. UberEats does not share the customer's phone number. Instead, a masking proxy phone number
  is provided to keep the customer's phone number confidential. When a retailer dials this number, they're required to enter an access code
  for their call to be put through to the end customer. On UberEats orders, this proxy phone number and access code are accessible at the
  `thirdPartyFacilitatorData.uberEats.proxyPhoneNumber` and `thirdPartyFacilitatorData.uberEats.customerPhoneCode` fields.
* UberEats orders share a very restricted set of customer details, which can complicate customer recording concerns. Some differences include:
  * Customer name as first name and last initial only
  * No email address
  * Phone numbers do not belong to customers and are not unique across UberEats orders

### Other Call Outs
* **Leafly Order UI set to read only**: The Leafly Order Dashboard will become read-only, as your software system will become the source of truth for order statuses and cart totals.
* **Third Party Delivery**: The behavior of the API will change if a retailer activates a third-party delivery integration (e.g., Onfleet).
  This shifts the source of truth for the delivery lifecycle to the delivery integration. If a retailer is using both an order integration with your point-of-sale and a delivery integration at the same time, the order API will no longer accept updates to delivery statuses, and will instead receive updates from the delivery integration, then send them to you in the form of a webhook.
* **Shared URL domain for all retailers associated with your system**: URLs associated with your retailer partners should all share the same URL domain. Unique per-retailer URL domains are not supported. The `orderIntegrationKey` uniquely identifies each retailer.
* **Dynamic request metadata is not supported**: Leafly does not support custom or dynamic IDs, params, or HTTP headers.

### Preparing for Production
Graduating your integration from the sandbox development environment to production requires demonstrating the
  quality and completeness of your integration. At a minimum your integration should be able to smoothly and
  reliably move orders from inception to completion for both terminal states ([`picked_up`, `canceled`]) and both
  fulfillment mechanisms ([`pickup`, `delivery`]).

It's not required to build against all elements of the API, though it is encouraged to provide the most value to our mutual
  retailers and shoppers. The table below summarizes which components of the Order API are mandatory, which are strongly encouraged, and which are considered optional.

| API Element                  | Type     | Expectation - validated by review of logged activity                | Requirement    | Value Add of Recommended Features                                           |
|------------------------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Retailer Activation         | Webhook  | 200 Ok, empty response bodies                                        | _Optional_     | Opportunity to gate retailer activation                                     |
| Retailer Deactivation        | Webhook  | 200 Ok, empty response bodies                                       | _Optional_     | Notifies your integration of retailer deactivation                          |
| Order Preview                | Webhook  | 200 Ok, response bodies matching the specification of this document | _Recommended_  | Pricing/stocking surprise-free shopping experience for our mutual customers |
| Order Submission             | Webhook  | 200 Ok, empty response bodies                                       | **_Required_** |                                                                             |
| Order Cancelation            | Webhook  | 200 Ok, empty response bodies                                       | **_Required_** |                                                                             |
| Order Status                 | Webhook  | 200 Ok, empty response bodies                                       | _Recommended_  | Keeps your integration synchronized with 3rd party delivery lifecycle       |
| Fetch Order by ID            | Endpoint | Successful retrievals                                               | **_Required_** |                                                                             |
| Retrieve Government ID Image | Endpoint | Successful retrievals                                               | _Recommended_  | Safety enhancement for retailers without needing to view LeaflyBiz          |
| Retrieve Medical ID Image    | Endpoint | Successful retrievals                                               | _Recommended_  | Compliance enhancement for retailers without needing to view LeaflyBiz      |
| Acknowledge Order            | Endpoint | Successful requests                                                 | **_Required_** |                                                                             |
| Update Order Status          | Endpoint | Successful motion through order lifecycles                          | **_Required_** |                                                                             |
| Update Order's Cart          | Endpoint | Successful updates of cart contents, taxes, delivery fees           | _Optional_     | Synchronization of final order state between systems                        |

When you're confident your integration is ready to advance to production please contact API Support at **api-support@leafly.com**,
  or feel free to reach out through other channels we may have configured with your team.

### Getting Help
For technical issues with the API or questions regarding this documentation, please contact API Support at
**api-support@leafly.com**.

For access requests, production ramp-up, or other operational questions, please contact our Partner Ops Team at
**partners@leafly.com**.

### Sharing Feedback
If you have suggestions for how the Leafly Order API or this documentation can be improved, please share your ideas with us by submitting **[this form](https://puqwdu2b3oa.typeform.com/to/RW35JZgD)**

get.description: Fetch the binary representing the government id image the customer submitted with their order. This endpoint is only usable prior to order acknowledgement and only when the order is in pending status.
Fetch the binary representing the medical id image the customer submitted with their order. This endpoint is only usable prior to order acknowledgement and only when the order is in pending status.

post.description:
This endpoint confirms that your system has retrieved all necessary details regarding an order,
including any associated media (e.g., government and medical id images).
- Acknowledgement of order receipt is required before any changes can be made to that order
through other API operations
- Once an order has been acknowledged, access to an order's associated media is revoked.

Move an order along its lifecycle by advancing its status.
- Updates to order status are only available after an order has been acknowledged
- Order statuses can only be moved forward
- Orders cannot be moved from their current status to the same status
- Orders cannot be moved out of a terminal status (`picked_up`, `canceled`, `expired`)
- Orders cannot be moved to 'pending' or 'expired' status with this endpoint

There may not be a one-to-one mapping of your system's statuses with those of Leafly's, so issuing updates using every status is not required.
However it is expected that the status updates issued are a best-approximation as can be allowed by the status mapping between the two systems,
and that they result in a reasonably smooth and intuitive order lifecycle for the end shopper.

Updating an order's status to `canceled` allows for the optional inclusion of a `cancelationReasonCode`. This endpoint will accept all
cancelation reason codes described in this document with the exception of `order_api_unacknowledged`. If no reason is provided the value of
`cancelationReasonCode` will default to `dispensary`.

![Statuses Flow Chart](https://docs.leafly.io/reservations-api/order-api/images/order-status-diagram.png)

Declaratively change an order by supplying a new state for its cart items and taxes.

Supported cart item operations are item additions, removals, substitutions, and a specific set of edits (which manifest as substitutions).
  Changes are applied as an all-succeed or all-fail transaction. Changes made to cart items will trigger a recalculation of order
  discounts and totals.

Custom values supplied for the `quantity` and `packagePrice` properties will be respected during additions and substitutions.
  All other values are sourced from Leafly's catalog using the `integratorVariantId` to lookup item information supplied
  by your integration to the [Leafly Menu API](https://docs.leafly.io/menu-integration-docs/v1.1.html). If the `integratorVariantId`
  references a non-existent or out-of-stock item the request will be rejected.

Additions are applied by including a new entry in the `cartItems` array with a `null` value for the `id` property.
  The `integratorVariantId` will be used to populate the details of the added item(s), the value supplied for `quantity`
  will be applied and the value supplied for `packagePrice` will override the price found in the Leafly catalog.

Removals are applied by leaving an item absent from the new `cartItems[]` array.

Substitutions are applied by changing the value of `integratorVariantId` while leaving the `id` value the same. As with additions,
  the `quantity` and `packagePrice` properties will be respected, with other properties referenced according to the new
  `integratorVariantId` value. After checkout, cart items are immutable, so the operation results in the insertion of a new entry
  into `cartItems[]` which will have a new `id` value, with the affected cart item being removed. The principal difference
  between this operation as compared to a combined addition and removal is the order log will record a substitution instead of
  a separate addition and removal.

Edits can be applied by changing the value of `quantity` or `packagePrice` on existing entries in `cartItems`. These changes will
  manifest as a substitution, where the affected item will be removed from `cartItems[]` and a new item will be introduced in its
  place.

Any specific variant id can only appear on one cart item. Updates where multiple cart items refer to the same variant will be
  rejected.

Changes made to `packagePrice` should reflect only the top-line, before-discount price of affected items. Introducing pricing
  reflecting discounts not known by Leafly's deal editor is likely to produce reconciliation headaches for our mutual customers.

The supplied array of taxes will replace the existing taxes on the order.

This webhook is called when a retailer attempts to activate the ordering integration with your platform from LeaflyBiz. Returning an error to the webhook
request will prevent the integration from being turned on, so you may use it to gate retailer activation as might be necessary.

requestBody.description: Metadata identifying the retailer enabling the integration.

200.description: Your server returns this code if it accepts the activation callback.

post.description:
This webhook is called when a retailer deactivates the ordering integration with your platform from LeaflyBiz. Deactivation will proceed regardless of the
response to the webhook request.

requestBody.description: Metadata identifying the retailer disabling the integration.

200.description: Your server returns this code if it accepts the deactivation callback.

post.description:
This webhook is dispatched at key checkpoints during the Leafly shopping funnel where validation of
item availability, pricing, and taxation on a shopper's cart are a large value add to the experience
of the shopper. At these junctures our platform will call out to your integration with a
summarized representation of the user's cart contents and fulfillment intentions. The preview webhook
expects a synchronous response with a further distilled representation of the cart where your integration
has an opportunity to adjust items quantities (downward only), remove items entirely, correct
top-of-line pricing, and supply a list of applicable taxes.

requestBody.description: The cart is included in the webhook callback.

post.description: This webhook is dispatched when an order is created on Leafly.

requestBody.description: Contains metadata about the newly submitted order.

200.description: Your server returns this code if it accepts the order submit callback.

post.description: This webhook is dispatched when an order is canceled.

requestBody.description: Contains metadata about the canceled order.

200.description: Your server returns this code if it accepts the order cancel callback.

post.description:
This webhook is dispatched when an order status changes. This is typically only
  relevant if part of the order lifecycle needs to be managed outside of your
  platform. For example, if a retailer is using a separate integration to manage
  deliveries through a third party.

requestBody.description: Contains metadata about the order with the status change.

200.description: Your server returns this code if it accepts the order status change callback.

OAuth2ClientCredentials.description:
The Leafly Order API uses OAuth 2 with the client credentials flow for inbound requests.
  The token url for the sandbox environment is `https://sso-sandbox.leafly.io/token`

WebhookHMACAuthentication.name: X-Leafly-Signature
WebhookHMACAuthentication.description:
Webhooks outbound from Leafly will include an `X-Leafly-Signature` header representing
  an `HMAC-SHA-256` digest of the request body using an HMAC key issued to you alongside
  your client credentials for this purpose. Authenticate webhooks received from Leafly by
  independently computing the HMAC signature from the request body and your HMAC key, then
  comparing the result with the value present in the header.

id.description: string identifier of this cart item

integratorVariantId.description: id assigned by your system to the variant when submitted through Leafly Menu API. It is very important that this id was given, otherwise it will resolve to the identifier of the parent menu item - introducing ambiguity likely to cause reconciliation problems for our mutual customers.

quantity.description: number of instances of this item that have been ordered

packagePrice.description: top line price per quantity of cart item in minor units

name.description: name of menu item associated with this cart item

brandName.description: name of the brand associated with the menu item

integratorVariantId.description: id assigned to variant when submitted through Leafly Menu API, if no variant id was given, this will resolve to the id of the parent menu item

quantity.description: number of instances of this item that have been ordered

packageUnit.description: unit of measurement applied to the menu item, e.g., "g", "mg", "pc", "each", etc

packageSize.description: instances of `packageUnit` making up a package, e.g., "1.0" paired with `packageUnit` "g", etc

packagePrice.description: original price per quantity of cart item in minor units

discountedPackagePrice.description: price per quantity of cart item in minor units after discount application

discountedPriceCents.description: price of entire cart item (all quantity) in minor units after discount application

dealTitle.description: the name of the retailer-defined deal when applicable

priceCents.description: original price of entire cart item (all quantity) in minor units

savingsCents.description: difference between original and discounted price of entire cart item (all quantity) in minor units

DeliveryAddress.description: Required if fulfillmentMechanism is set to `delivery`.

FulfillmentMechanism.description: how the customer intends to receive their order

eventTime.description: timestamp of when the event occurred

orderIntegrationKey.description: identifier of the retailer associated with the event

MedicalStatus.description: whether the order is medical or recreational, generally only applies to orders placed in the United States

timeZone.description: IANA timezone applicable to the order

cancelationReason.description: human friendly reason for order cancelation

subtotal.description: order total before taxes and fees in minor units

deliveryFee.description: order delivery fee in minor units. Must be zero for pickup orders.

tip.description: total tip applied to the order in minor units. Returns 0 when no tip was provided.

totalDiscounts.description: total of discounts applied to the order in minor units

total.description: order grand total in minor units, after aggregating all items, taxes, fees, and discounts. Tip is not included. For example, a `subtotal` of `2000`, `deliveryFee` of `1000`, `taxes` totaling `1000`, and totalDiscounts of `1500` will have a `total` of `2500`.

totalWithTip.description: order grand total including tip in minor units, after aggregating all items, taxes, fees, discounts, and tip. Returns the same value as `total` when no tip was provided.

deliveryAddress.description: the order's delivery destination if applicable

scheduled.description: whether this order is scheduled for fulfillment during a specific window. At present can only apply to delivery orders.

statusChanges.description: history of the order's status changes

taxes.description: Summary of tax line items applied to the order

deliveryFee.description: order delivery fee in minor units. Must be zero for pickup orders.

taxes.description: Summary of tax line items applied to the order

customerPhoneCode.description: Access code to contact an UberEats customer by phone

proxyPhoneNumber.description:
A non-unique proxy phone number provided by UberEats that masks the customer's
real phone number. This number can be used in conjunction with the `customerPhoneCode`
to place a call that will be connected to the end customer. This phone number
does not belong to and is not unique to the customer.
